source_text: Caeterum, si quae audent interserere se aetati apostolicae, ut ideo videantur ab Apostolis traditae, quia sub Apostolis fuerunt, possumus dicere: Edant ergo origines Ecclesiarum suarum: evolvant ordinem episcoporum suorum, ita per successiones ab initio decurrentem, ut primus ille episcopus aliquem ex Apostolis, vel apostolicis viris, qui tamen cum Apostolis perseveraverit, habuerit auctorem et antecessorem. Hoc enim modo Ecclesiae apostolicae census suos deferunt: sicut Smyrnaeorum Ecclesia Polycarpum ab Joanne conlocatum refert: sicut Romanorum, Clementem a Petro ordinatum edit; proinde utique et caeterae exhibent quos ab Apostolis in episcopatum constitutos apostolici seminis traduces habeant. Confingant tale aliquid Haeretici. Quid enim illis post blasphemiam inlicitum est? Sed etsi confinxerint, nihil promovebunt. Ipsa enim doctrina eorum cum apostolica comparata, ex diversitate et contrarietate sua pronuntiabit, neque apostoli alicujus auctoris esse, neque apostolici; quia sicut Apostoli non diversa inter se docuissent, ita et apostolici non contraria Apostolis edidissent, nisi illi qui ab Apostolis didicerunt aliter praedicaverunt. Ad hanc itaque formam probabuntur ab illis ecclesiis, quae licet nullum ex Apostolis, vel apostolicis, auctorem suum proferant, ut multo posteriores, quae denique quotidie instituuntur; tamen in eadem fide conspirantes, non minus apostolicae deputantur, pro consanguinitate doctrinae. Ita omnes haereses ad utramque formam nostris Ecclesiis provocatae, probent se quaqua putant apostolicas. Sed adeo nec sunt, nec probare possunt quod non sunt, nec recipiuntur in pacem et communicationem ab Ecclesiis quoquo modo apostolicis, scilicet ob diversitatem sacramenti nullo modo apostolicae.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover, if some dare to insert themselves into the apostolic age, so that they may seem to have been handed down by the Apostles, because they were under the Apostles, we can say: Let them therefore produce the origins of their Churches; let them unfold the order of their bishops, in such a way that it flows down through successions from the beginning, so that the first bishop may have had some Apostle, or apostolic men who nevertheless persevered with the Apostles, as author and predecessor. For in this way the apostolic Churches bring forth their own census: just as the Church of the Smyrnaeans reports that Polycarp was placed by John, just as the Romans produce Clement as ordained by Peter; likewise, the other Churches also exhibit those who were constituted by the Apostles in the episcopate, as having apostolic seed. Let the Heretics fabricate something of this kind. For what is forbidden to them after blasphemy? But even if they fabricate, they will accomplish nothing. For their own doctrine, compared with the apostolic doctrine, will declare from its diversity and contrariness that they are not of any apostolic author, nor apostolic; because just as the Apostles did not teach diverse things among themselves, so also the apostolic men did not teach things contrary to the Apostles, unless those who learned from the Apostles preached otherwise. Therefore, they will be proven by those Churches which, although they do not produce any Apostle, or apostolic man, as their author, as much later, which are finally established daily; nevertheless, conspiring in the same faith, they are not less considered apostolic, by reason of the consanguinity of doctrine. Thus, all heresies, provoked by our Churches to both forms, let them prove themselves to be apostolic, as they think. But not even are they, nor can they prove what they are not, nor are they received into peace and communion by the Churches in any way apostolic, namely because of the diversity of the sacrament in no way apostolic.
pass_b_english: If anyone dares to wedge themselves into the apostolic era just so they can claim the Apostles handed them down—on the grounds that they ‘lived under the Apostles’—we can answer bluntly: let them cough up the origins of their churches. Let them lay out the full line of their bishops, an unbroken succession from the very start, so that their first bishop can name an Apostle—or at least an apostolic man who stuck with the Apostles—as his author and predecessor. That is exactly how the apostolic churches present their credentials: the church of Smyrna records that John installed Polycarp; the Romans produce Clement, ordained by Peter. In the same way, every other church displays the men the Apostles themselves appointed to the episcopate, the living carriers of apostolic seed. Let the heretics try to fabricate a list like that. After blasphemy, what is left that they would not dare? Yet even if they concoct one, it will get them nowhere. Their own teaching, set beside the apostolic teaching, will shout from its very contradictions that they have no apostolic author and are not apostolic. The Apostles never disagreed among themselves, so apostolic men never taught anything contrary to the Apostles—unless those who learned from the Apostles turned around and preached something else. Therefore, churches that cannot name an Apostle or apostolic man as their founder, churches that came much later and are still being planted every day, are nevertheless judged apostolic because they conspire in the same faith; the kinship of doctrine makes them family. So every heresy, challenged by our churches on both counts, let them prove themselves apostolic if they think they can. But they are not, they cannot prove what they are not, and they are not welcomed into peace or communion by any church that is in any way apostolic—precisely because their sacrament differs in a way that is anything but apostolic.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful formal translation, and Pass B provides a more idiomatic rendering that preserves all nuances of the original, including the jussive moods and the causal relations. All clauses, including the specific examples of Polycarp/John and Clement/Peter, are present and correctly rendered. The title 'Apostolic Succession' accurately reflects the thought of the passage.
